title: Adaptive Information Processing Model
subtitle: EMDR’s clinical model of insufficiently integrated memory
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating adaptive information processing model across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
learningObjectives: Explain adaptive information processing model in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in adaptive information processing model.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to adaptive information processing model.

sections.explainSimply: AIP proposes that some distress persists when experiences remain stored in maladaptive forms and are not integrated with adaptive information.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: It guides case conceptualisation and target selection, but it is a psychotherapy model rather than a directly verified neural-storage theory.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Use the model pragmatically while maintaining differential diagnosis and evidence-based risk management.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of adaptive information processing model as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need adaptive information processing model to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Do not present “blocked processing” as a measurable brain lesion.
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use adaptive information processing model to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses adaptive information processing model to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Do not present “blocked processing” as a measurable brain lesion. Evidence classification: clinical theoretical model.
